classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that each connecting line corresponds to an unordered pair of distinct points.

content.prompt: Suppose 11 points are arranged around a circle. How many straight lines must be drawn so that every point is connected to every other point?

spec.description: Eleven black marked points placed around a circle, with a straight segment joining every distinct pair. There are no labels, additional intersection markers, filled regions or separate circumference stroke.
spec.mathematics: Complete pairwise connectivity on 11 distinct boundary points. Interior intersections are not additional given points.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete connecting diagram is supplied in the student question; no numerical answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Each line joins an unordered pair of distinct points.
$$\begin{align*}
\binom{11}{2}&=\frac{11!}{2!9!}\\
\binom{11}{2}&=\frac{11\times10}{2}\\
\binom{11}{2}&=55.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore, 55 lines must be drawn.
